themeDesignLanguage: Plain undyed-to-mid-brown boiled and oiled leather: simple panelled hide, visible saddle stitching, plain iron buckles and rivets, coarse linen or wool backing where cloth is needed - plain undyed oatmeal, grey or brown homespun, never dyed, patterned or trimmed. Utterly unornamented - no engraving, filigree, heraldry, gemstones, gilding, fur trim, or maker marks. Metal appears only as functional fittings and blade/head stock: plain grey iron, matte and slightly pitted, never polished, never brass or steel-blue. Wood is bare ash or oak, oiled, straight-grained, no carving or inlay. Small personal fittings - rings, buckles, toggles and clasps - are plain forged iron bands and loops of the same utilitarian stock as the buckles on the armour: worn as practical kit, never as jewellery, with no stone, no engraving and no precious metal. Silhouettes are the textbook generic form of each item as a player would picture it from the name alone: light, flexible, quiet gear for rogues, rangers, bards, hunters and scouts who wear leather rather than plate. Excludes: plate armour, chainmail, magic glow, sci-fi materials, modern fasteners, and any decorative flourish whatsoever.
